belief: If I had enough faith, God would heal me.
origins: Some teachers and friends say that healing depends on the size of our faith. When healing does not come, guilt and doubt pile on top of illness.
teaches: Jesus responded to faith that was weak: the father cried, “I do believe; help my unbelief!” and Jesus healed his son (Mark 9:24). Paul prayed three times about his thorn, and God said, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Timothy had frequent ailments, Epaphroditus was sick “nearly unto death,” and Paul left Trophimus “sick in Miletus.” Scripture treats illness as part of life, not as a faith failure. God can and does heal, and He does so by His wisdom, not by a formula.
self_statements: God is waiting for me to believe more.
It is my fault I am not healed.
I am blocking my own healing.
errors: Believing healing is either by faith or never.
Predicting that I will stay sick.
Feeling unhealed and concluding that my faith is weak.
questions: Who taught me that healing depends on faith?
What did Jesus do with weak faith?
What did Paul and others do when healing did not come?
What does grace look like in my situation?
How can I trust God without a guarantee?
What care can I receive in the meantime?
truth: My healing does not depend on the size of my faith. God hears even weak faith, and His grace is sufficient. I can ask for healing, receive medical care, and trust Him with the outcome.
hw_truths: I can trust God with the outcome.
log: Each week, note one prayer and one act of trust.
actions: Notice Jesus’ response to weak faith.
Talk with a pastor if guilt persists.
prayer: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief. Heal as You see fit, and give me grace in the meantime. Amen.
